🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Bobby Wright, the actor and country singer who played radio operator Willy Moss on the 1960s hit sitcom McHale's Navy and was the son of country music legend Kitty Wells, has died at 84.

Wright died Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at his home in Madison, Tennessee, his family announced. According to his family's obituary, he passed away peacefully surrounded by loved ones. No cause of death has been publicly reported.

Born John Robert Wright Jr. on March 30, 1942, in Charleston, West Virginia, Wright grew up in a country music family. His mother was Kitty Wells, country music's first female superstar and a member of the Country Music Hall of Fame, and his father was Johnnie Wright, half of the duo Johnnie & Jack. As a boy, Wright sang with his parents on the Louisiana Hayride program and played guitar, and the family moved to Nashville in 1958 when his parents became headliners at the Grand Ole Opry.

Wright went to Hollywood to audition for a television role as a young Southerner who could play guitar. That show did not move forward, but his screen test was seen by a producer on McHale's Navy, who cast him as Willy Moss, the PT-73 radio operator — billed as John Wright on the show. The ABC comedy, starring Ernest Borgnine, Joe Flynn and Tim Conway and set aboard a Navy boat in the Pacific during World War II, ran for four seasons from 1962 to 1966, and Wright appeared on all 138 episodes. He reprised the role in the big-screen spinoffs McHale's Navy (1964) and McHale's Navy Joins the Air Force (1966).

After the series ended, Wright returned to music. He recorded for Decca, ABC and United Artists Records from 1967 to 1979 and placed 21 singles on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart, with "Here I Go Again" peaking at No. 13 in 1971. He also performed for years with his parents and sisters on the syndicated Kitty Wells Johnnie Wright Family Show and toured with his parents until they retired from the road in 2007. He was the last surviving cast member of the McHale's Navy television series.

He is survived by his sister Carol Sue; his children, LeAnn and Kamela; his grandchildren; and his great-grandchildren.

Sources: The Hollywood Reporter; family obituary.
